title: A loyalty platform's own OAuth authorization server, serving a public mobile client and confidential partner apps
provenance: Synthetic system authored for this corpus (issue #744). Not derived from, or sanitized from, any real system: there is nothing to leak by omission.
notes: Holdout case 1 of 2 for #744. It fills three gaps at once: the corpus's first ASVS level 3 case, the first case where we run the OAuth authorization server ourselves, and the first where a session and a token are two different things with two different lifetimes. The support-console finding joins three stated facts no one sentence holds: the rewards API checks no audience, one key signs tokens for the API and for the support console, and the console sits on the same public hostname. It stays conditional, because the source states neither the console's audience check nor its role check. Level 3 is what turns two stated values into gaps: a ten-minute authorization code and plain bearer tokens are both acceptable at level 2. Held out of tuning: no diagnosis reads it, so it confirms a fix measured on the other cases.
